title: VisualRecipe
description:
A saved COMBINATION, not a saved prompt. The brief is explicit: a Visual Recipe stores the entire reference combination - which references, which attributes were taken from each, how conflicts were resolved, and the resulting intent - so it can be reopened, re-edited and re-explored. Re-running formatPrompt on a recipe reproduces the prompt; the reverse is impossible, which is exactly why a recipe is not a prompt preset.

SELF-CONTAINMENT: `references` holds full ReferenceSnapshots including license, creator and attribution, so a shared recipe stays attributable even when the recipient has none of those references in their own library and even when the provider is unreachable.

MEDIA URL ROT - the policy, in five rules:
  R1. IDENTITY IS NOT A URL. The durable identity of a work is (metadata.source, metadata.source_id) plus metadata.source_url. metadata.media_url is a CACHE HINT and is expected to rot.
  R2. A ROTTED RECIPE STILL WORKS. Intent, mix, conflict resolutions and every taxonomy id are pixel-free, so a recipe with 100% dead media still produces the same prompt. Media loss degrades the CARD, never the RECIPE.
  R3. RESOLUTION ORDER. resolveMedia(snapshot): (1) HEAD metadata.media_url; on success set media_state='ok'. (2) On failure call provider(source).getMetadata(source_id) and, if a new URL comes back, store it in resolved_media_url and set media_state='moved'. (3) On failure set media_state='gone' and keep the record.
  R4. ATTRIBUTION SURVIVES. metadata.attribution is stored TEXT, never a computed link, so credit is never erased by a dead URL. A 'gone' snapshot still renders its full credit line.
  R5. NO REHYDRATION BY COPYING BYTES. Rot is never fixed by embedding the image - binaries are never stored (see reference.schema.json). The offered remedies are re-resolve, open source_url, or replace the reference (which is a recipe EDIT and bumps `version`).

schema_version.description: Version of the SCHEMA (MAJOR.MINOR). Distinct from `version`, which versions the recipe's CONTENT.

id.description: rcp_<slug>. Stable for the life of the recipe across every content revision.

version.description: Monotonic CONTENT revision. Incremented on any change to intent, mix or references. Two recipes with the same id and version MUST be byte-identical in those three fields.

created_by.description: Author handle or identifier. Free-form; the product stores no account model.

intent.description: The resolved VisualIntent at save time, in full chip form so per-chip provenance (which reference gave what) survives sharing.

mix.description: The reference combination, including per-entry use/weight/priority/pin and the conflict resolutions. This is the part a prompt preset cannot express.

references.description: Full metadata snapshots of every reference the mix touches. INV-RCP-1: every mix.references[].reference_id MUST have a snapshot here, so the recipe is standalone. Snapshots are frozen copies: editing the live library never silently rewrites a saved recipe.

prompt_mode.description: Formatter target saved with the recipe. A recipe can be re-rendered in any other mode without editing it.

prompt_preview.description: Optional cached render, kept purely so a recipe list can show text without loading the taxonomy. ADVISORY: on open, the prompt is always re-derived from intent + mix; if the re-derived text differs (taxonomy moved on, a node was deprecated) the UI shows a 'regenerated' notice rather than trusting the cache.

cover_reference_id.description: Which snapshot's thumbnail represents the recipe. Falls back to the first snapshot whose media_state is not 'gone'.

license_summary.description: Aggregated licence position of the whole recipe, computed from the snapshots at save time and recomputed on load. Lets a recipient see, before using it, what obligations they inherit. NOTE: this describes the REFERENCE MEDIA only; it says nothing about the licence of the code or of the generated output. Reference licensing and code licensing are separate concerns and are never conflated.

share_alike.description: True when any snapshot is cc_by_sa.

has_excluded.description: True when any snapshot carries an excluded-by-default licence. A recipe with has_excluded=true MUST warn on open and MUST NOT be exported by default.

attribution_block.description: Ready-to-paste credit text: one line per snapshot, built from stored attribution strings so it is immune to URL rot.

integrity.description: Optional tamper/drift detection. No media bytes are hashed - only the recipe's own structured content.

content_hash.description: sha256 over canonical-JSON(intent, mix, references, prompt_mode). Detects silent edits and lets two copies be compared without a diff.

taxonomy_version.description: Taxonomy revision the recipe was authored against. On load, ids missing from the current taxonomy are rewritten via replaced_by, or kept as custom chips with a 'deprecated node' badge - never dropped.

media_health.description: Rollup of the last resolveMedia() sweep across the snapshots. Purely informational; a recipe is never invalidated by it.

exports.description: Non-prompt outputs derived from this recipe (brief, Future: storyboard description, shot list, image prompt, video prompt). Derived and regenerable; never the source of truth.

kind.description: The first four are exactly the ComfyUI node's outputs, so the node and the web app export the same things.
